newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai, HK bourses seen separate, cooperating.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai, HK bourses seen separate, cooperating.

text.p: The Shanghai and Hong Kong stock exchanges should cooperate but operate independently after the British colony reverts to China on July 1, the president of the Shanghai bourse was quoted on Wednesday as saying.

"After Hong Kong returns to China, the two bourses will expand cooperation and mutual exchanges under the precondition that they work separately," Yang Xianghai was quoted as saying by the Shanghai Securities News.
Yang said the Shanghai bourse would continue to be the key channel through which Chinese firms raise money by issuing stocks and cooperate bonds and by trading state debt.

The Hong Kong exchange in its turn will become the best channel for major Chinese companies to seek funding outside China, Yang told a visiting Hong Kong economic delegation headed by Victor Fung, chairman of the Hong Kong Trade Development Council.

Alex Tsui, chief executive of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, said the two exchanges had discussed further cooperation including training, information exchanges and developing China's foreign currency B share markets, the newspaper said.
At the meeting, some members of the delegation expressed the hope that Hong Kong firms could go to the Shanghai bourse for secondary listings, the newspaper said.
"The Hong Kong exchange is willing to cooperate with the Shanghai exchange to actively promote the process," Alex Tsui was quoted as saying.
